qualitative.filing_summary_10k: For fiscal 2026 (ended January 31, 2026), TJX reported net sales of $60.4 billion, up 7% from $56.4 billion, with consolidated comp sales up 5% and diluted EPS of $4.87 versus $4.26 a year earlier. Pre-tax margin improved to 12.1% from 11.5%, aided partly by a $419 million net gain from a credit card interchange fee litigation settlement recorded in SG&A, offset by related one-time compensation expenses. The filing also discusses ongoing uncertainty around U.S. tariffs, including a Supreme Court ruling invalidating certain IEEPA tariffs followed by a new executive order imposing a global tariff, and notes store count grew about 3% with continued expansion planned across all segments in fiscal 2027.
qualitative.filing_summary_8k: This 8-K discloses that on September 16, 2026, TJX's Board of Directors elected Craig A. Pintoff, an Executive Vice President and Chief Administrative Officer at United Rentals, Inc., as a new independent director and member of the Audit and Finance Committee, effective immediately. The filing describes his compensation under the company's standard non-employee director program and states there are no related-party transactions or arrangements connected to his appointment.
qualitative.moat_explanation: The 10-K describes a low-cost operating structure (lean advertising spend, no-frills store fixtures, cost-effective distribution) combined with an opportunistic buying strategy leveraging roughly 21,000 global vendors and substantial buying power to acquire brand-name merchandise at prices 20%-60% below full-price retailers. This scale-driven, flexible sourcing and inventory model is presented as a structural cost and pricing advantage versus traditional retailers, though the filing also notes larger competitors with greater resources.
red_flags: Company acknowledges it operates in 'highly competitive markets' against larger, better-resourced competitors and 'may not be able to compete effectively'

Heavy reliance on merchandise sourced from China, India, and southeastern Asia exposes the company to tariffs, trade restrictions, and supply chain disruption risks explicitly discussed in Risk Factors

Tariff uncertainty is called out as an ongoing issue, including a Supreme Court ruling invalidating certain IEEPA tariffs followed by a new executive order imposing different tariffs, creating unresolved uncertainty for cost structure

Fiscal 2026 results benefited from a one-time $419 million net gain from a credit card interchange fee litigation settlement, which inflates period-over-period margin and EPS comparisons and is not a recurring business driver
General corporate expense increased in fiscal 2026 due to higher administrative costs and settlement-related expenses
